subject.title: api_key auth: MRU sticky ordering + silent 402 failover

question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit MRU/failover-only auth-profile routing mode for API-key pools, or keep oldest-first round-robin as the only automatic default?
rationale: The requested behavior changes provider auth selection, fallback visibility, and likely public config semantics; automation should not choose those defaults without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add opt-in MRU or failover-only mode
options.body: Preserve current round-robin behavior by default while adding a documented policy mode for users who want the last successful profile preferred after reset or failover.

options.title: Change API-key default to MRU
options.body: Make the reporter's preferred behavior automatic for API-key profiles, accepting compatibility risk for users relying on load distribution.

options.title: Defer to broader pool-routing design
options.body: Keep this issue open as input to a broader provider-profile routing policy before adding another auth knob.

recommendation.title: Add opt-in MRU or failover-only mode
recommendation.body: Preserve current round-robin behavior by default while adding a documented policy mode for users who want the last successful profile preferred after reset or failover.

likelyOwner.reason: The blocking choice is auth/config product direction across provider routing, and steipete has the strongest recent history on those boundaries among the identified owners.
